answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce token stake before it may post offers, then slash that stake when independently verified trades reveal fraud. A single operator can still create many identities, but each one ties up capital and risks losing it; splitting a fixed budget across sybils also leaves each with less influence and earning capacity. This does not make identities unique: it makes mass deception costly, whether the accounts gather at lagoon, cross a dune, or claim ivory.
